plans.note: Section 9 is the dedicated limitation of liability clause; check mutuality, cap amount/formula and carve-outs, and cross-read the indemnity (sec-8-2) and warranty disclaimer (sec-8) for any liability exclusions that undercut the cap.

Section 8 (INDEMNIFICATION) should carry Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; confirm scope, defence/control, and that any reciprocal Corio indemnity stays narrow. Check sec-9 for a cap applied to the indemnity.

Defined terms CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY suggest field-of-use or market restrictions in the grant of rights (sec-3) and definitions (sec-1-2); also scan SHARED RESOURCES (sec-13) and miscellaneous for competitive-activity limits on us.

Look for exclusive-sourcing or preferred-provider language in the grant of rights and in the Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation terms; if only Commerce One is restricted, that benefits us and is not flagged.
Pricing (Exhibit B), fees and payment terms are the only plausible homes for a most-favoured-customer clause; likely absent, and if present in our favour it should not be redlined.
No dedicated personnel clause in the outline; check MISCELLANEOUS and the confidentiality section for a buried non-solicit binding Corio, otherwise treat as absent.

Section 11 (TERM AND TERMINATION) governs; check whether Corio has a convenience right with reasonable notice and no penalty, and whether Commerce One can terminate mid-term or accelerate fees on exit.
Initial term, renewal mechanics and notice window sit in sec-11; cross-check Exhibit B pricing for renewal-period uplift or repricing terms.
Governing law, venue and any dispute mechanism (the defined term RULES hints at arbitration) will be in MISCELLANEOUS; verify the chosen law is an accepted one and that any arbitration is domestic.

Assignment/change-of-control language is normally in MISCELLANEOUS; confirm we may assign to affiliates and successors and that a Corio change of control does not give Commerce One a termination right (check sec-11 too).

DEVELOPMENTS and EMPLOYEE NDA/INVENTION AGREEMENT are defined, so ownership allocation likely sits in the grant of rights and definitions; check whether Corio-created developments, configurations or customer data are assigned to Commerce One, and review the trademark and escrow sections for related IP terms.

Section 2 (GRANT OF RIGHTS) plus delivery and the Exhibit A software/demonstration software listings define scope; check revocability, territory, sublicensing to CUSTOMERS/SOFTWARE USERS, affiliates and contractors.
Revenue-sharing fees typically bring a records inspection right against Corio; look in FEES, Exhibit B payment terms and MISCELLANEOUS for frequency, notice, location and cost-bearing.
Check fees/payment terms for late-payment penalties or termination-triggered liquidated sums payable by Corio; service credits running to us are acceptable and not flagged.

Section 7 (WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER) with the defined Warranty Period and Acceptance Test governs duration and remedy; cross-read delivery/acceptance (sec-3) and maintenance (sec-5) for the repair-or-replace remedy.
No insurance heading in the outline; check MISCELLANEOUS and the indemnity section before concluding it is missing.
Exhibit B pricing and revenue-sharing fees are the likely source of any minimum guarantee or take-or-pay on Corio; confirm whether shortfalls are payable and whether an exit exists.

Check the effects-of-termination provisions in sec-11 for wind-down, continued service to existing CUSTOMERS and data return; the source code escrow (sec-12) is a partial continuity mechanism but is not a substitute for transition assistance.
